rationale: The literature consistently supports the absence of anterior temporal pole T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in pediatric and adolescent patients with biallelic loss-of-function (LoF) NOTCH3 variants, which sharply contrasts with classical CADASIL caused by heterozygous cysteine-altering variants. However, the hypothesis is conflicted regarding the spatial extent of neuroimaging pathology: white matter involvement is not strictly restricted to periventricular and periatrial regions. Several studies describe extensive cerebral white matter abnormalities, basal ganglia lacunar infarcts, microcalcifications, and brain atrophy in addition to periventricular patterns.

evidence.text: Three pediatric patients with biallelic cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 loss-of-function variants presented between 9 and 14 months with early-onset vascular leukoencephalopathy; MRI showed extensive cerebral white matter abnormalities, lacunes in the basal ganglia, microcalcifications, and atrophy, while the anterior temporal lobes were explicitly spared.

source.title: Early-onset vascular leukoencephalopathy caused by bi-allelic NOTCH3 variants
source.quote: MRI findings pointed at a small vessel disease, with extensive cerebral white matter abnormalities, atrophy, lacunes in the basal ganglia, microbleeds, and microcalcifications. The anterior temporal lobes were spared. Bi-allelic cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 variants in exons 1, 32, and 33 were found.

evidence.text: A proband with a homozygous NOTCH3 null variant (c.2984delC) showed livedo racemosa, ataxia, cognitive decline, seizures, and MRI white matter abnormalities without anterior temporal pole lesions, confirming that anterior temporal pole lesions are absent in biallelic loss-of-function variants.

source.title: Distinct neurological phenotypes associated with biallelic loss of NOTCH3 function: evidence for recessive inheritance
source.quote: Whole exome sequencing (WES) was performed on a proband who exhibited livedo racemosa, ataxia, cognitive decline, seizures, and MRI white matter abnormalities without anterior temporal pole lesions.

evidence.text: A 12-year-old patient with a homozygous frameshift variant in NOTCH3 (c.2985_2991del) presented with spastic tetraparesis, epilepsy, global developmental delay, and bilateral periventricular white matter abnormalities, expanding the spectrum of early-onset autosomal recessive leukodystrophy distinct from classical CADASIL.

source.title: A novel homozygous loss-of-function NOTCH3 variant in a Moroccan patient: expanding the spectrum beyond CADASIL
source.quote: We report a 12-year-old Moroccan girl, born to first-degree consanguineous parents, presenting with global developmental delay, spastic tetraparesis, epilepsy, and bilateral periventricular white matter abnormalities.

evidence.text: In monogenic cerebral small vessel disease cohorts, temporal pole hyperintensity is strongly characteristic of dominant cysteine-altering NOTCH3 mutations (up to 88.6% in high-risk EGFr domains) and contrasts with other variants, supporting temporal pole sparing as an atypical or non-CADASIL imaging pattern.

source.title: Comparison of clinical and imaging features of cerebral small vessel disease associated with heterozygous HTRA1 and NOTCH3 mutations
source.quote: Temporal pole involvement was most prevalent in NOTCH3 high-risk EGFr mutations (88.6%), followed by NOTCH3 moderate-risk EGFr mutations (32.4%), and least common in heterozygous HTRA1 mutations (28.6%).

evidence.text: Stellingwerff et al. explicitly demonstrated that leukoencephalopathy in biallelic NOTCH3 loss-of-function cases includes diffuse white matter abnormalities, basal ganglia lacunes, microcalcifications, and cerebral atrophy, contradicting the claim that pathology is restricted exclusively to periventricular and periatrial regions.

source.title: Early-onset vascular leukoencephalopathy caused by bi-allelic NOTCH3 variants
source.quote: MRI findings pointed at a small vessel disease, with extensive cerebral white matter abnormalities, atrophy, lacunes in the basal ganglia, microbleeds, and microcalcifications. The anterior temporal lobes were spared.

conflicts: While anterior temporal pole T2/FLAIR hyperintensity is consistently absent across all described pediatric and adolescent biallelic loss-of-function cohorts, white matter lesions and parenchymal pathology are not strictly restricted to the periventricular and periatrial zones; extensive cerebral white matter lesions, basal ganglia lacunes, and calcifications have been documented.

new_directions.question_text: What is the systematic neuroimaging distribution of subcortical versus deep white matter hyperintensities across all centrally reviewed biallelic NOTCH3 LoF patients using standardized visual rating scales?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether white matter volume loss and signal alterations are truly restricted to periatrial leukomalacia-like areas or routinely encompass deep frontal/parietal white matter will refine radiological criteria to discriminate recessive NOTCH3 disease from CADASIL and CARASIL.

new_directions.question_text: Do adult patients harboring biallelic null NOTCH3 mutations develop anterior temporal pole lesions later in life as a secondary consequence of chronic microvascular insufficiency?
new_directions.rationale: Testing longitudinal neuroimaging in homozygous LoF variant carriers into adulthood will determine whether anterior temporal pole sparing is a permanent lifelong hallmark or an age-dependent developmental feature.
